interpretation: The pinned public nvUvmInterface declarations allocate system memory in an RM VA space, map CPU access to that RM allocation, and duplicate it between RM VA spaces using an RM allocation address. The physical-memory duplicate API requires RM client and memory handles. No declared public interface prototype accepts Linux struct page, dma_addr_t, scatterlist, sg_table, or dma_buf descriptors. R580 also has a handle-based external allocation path: UVM accepts rmCtrlFd/hClient/hMemory, duplicates an RM object for a mapping GPU, and queries its PTEs. That path is a reuse candidate, but this source does not establish that one allocation handle can be imported across separate provider RM instances. The raw-descriptor result is only an API-surface gap; it does not prove that private RM internals or other handle-based paths cannot provide equivalent functionality, nor does it prove DMA visibility, ordering, coherence, or hardware behavior.
next_experiment: Prototype an explicit allocation-export/import contract that carries source-provider identity and creates a target-provider-local RM handle; test it with distinct provider handle tables before attempting a cross-GPU mapping. If no such RM import primitive is available, investigate a DMA-BUF-backed bridge with per-device DMA/IOMMU ownership, cache/order guarantees, unwind rules, and fault-progress tests before any module load.

cross_provider_import.classification_scope: pinned R580 UVM external-allocation path plus current hybrid UVM callback bridge
cross_provider_import.interpretation: The inspected UVM ioctl stores rmCtrlFd but does not pass it to DupMemory. The RM ABI receives a target device and raw client/memory handles; the hybrid bridge selects the target device's provider and forwards those handles without a source-provider identity. The later mapping route requires its VA space and duplicated handle to belong to the same provider. This identifies no source-owner/import route in these inspected paths; it does not prove all private RM or other DMA-BUF import mechanisms lack one.
